entries.text: The sheet and tracker may be wrong, but the ration is now recorded and it's about 7:21 AM. Say what Grukka does from the alders.

Before I answer, I have to flag a problem: the sheet and tracker shown to me don't match what happened at the table.

The status block lists a fight in round 8 against "Breach Bandits" and Harl. It also shows you prone at 8/15 HP with Rage spent, XP 175, and your greataxe, handaxes, javelins and Brother Aldric's satchel back in your pack. None of that happened, and the game record has no mention of any Breach Bandits. Your long rest finished cleanly at 7:01 AM, with no fight under way and your gear still inside the toll-house. I'm not going to play a fight that never occurred, and I'm not going to hand you gear you haven't recovered. I'm running the story as it was told: you're rested at full strength in the riverbank hollow, with the scimitar, the light crossbow and ten bolts.

Merra pulls her knees up and keeps her voice low. She saw little, since they kept her below, but she heard a lot through the floor. Gaunt arrived near midnight with two riders, and his deep, calm voice frightened Harl more than a shout would. She heard his name from Harl's mouth only once, and with a flinch. She also heard Gaunt say, almost kindly, "Then she's still out there. Good. Let her come. Strength that refuses to kneel is worth more to me than strength that obeys." He asked Pell about the temple's relic, and Pell stammered that it would be in the ledger. Merra doesn't know what relic he means.

You eat a ration (7 left), check the crossbow's string, and slip upstream through the reeds, leaving Merra hidden in the hollow. It's about 7:21 AM. From the alders you can see the yard: the wagons, the cookfire, Harl with his ribs bandaged and a sour look, six or seven grey sashes, and a bay horse with a bell on its harness tied by the stable. There's no sign of the man who owns it.

What does Grukka do?

Before I go further, I have to flag a problem with the record. The sheet and tracker shown to me this turn don't match what we just played.

- It shows a fight in round 8 against "Breach Bandits" and Harl, and I have no such fight in my notes. Our last scene ended with a long rest in the riverbank hollow, with no combat running.
- It shows Grukka at 8/15 HP, Prone, with Rage and Relentless Endurance spent. Our long rest restored them.
- It lists your greataxe, handaxes, javelins and Brother Aldric's satchel in your pack, plus 175 XP. In play, those are still inside the toll-house, and you've earned no XP yet.
- It's missing the light crossbow and bolts you took from Dunn.

I'm not going to resolve a fight I never ran, or hand you gear you haven't recovered, just because a status block says so. By everything we actually played, you are rested at 15/15 HP, with Rage 2/2 and Relentless Endurance 1/1. You hold a scimitar and a crossbow, and your weapons are still in the toll-house. If you remember it differently, tell me and we'll sort it out before anything else happens.

On that basis, here is what Merra tells you in the grey light, voice low and a little hoarse:

"I didn't see his face. They put me down here before he came, and the shutters were closed. But I heard the horse, and the bell on its harness, a little silver bell, wrong for a bandit. When he came in, nobody spoke for a long time. Harl said 'Master' and not 'Gaunt'. Then the man laughed softly and asked, 'And the big one? Dead?' Harl told him you'd run. He wasn't angry, Grukka. He said, 'Good. Let her come back. It's the temple I want, and she'll lead me to what's under it.' I don't know what's under it. I've served there four years, and there's only the crypt and the old well."

You eat a ration (that's one fewer), and the crossbow's string is sound. Smoke rises thin and steady from the alders upstream. Do you go and scout it as you said, and if so, should Merra stay hidden here or come with you?

entries.text:
Before the priestess can answer, the temple answers for her.

The barred door explodes inward off its hinges, and the nave fills with grey sashes. Two bandits pour through first, and Harl comes behind them with his mace already swinging. You're flat on the flagstones among splintered wood, your breath knocked out of you, prayer wheel still in your fist. The priestess stands over you with one hand raised, her lips moving in prayer, and the tracker shows the fight already several rounds old.

Here is where things stand, and I'm laying it out plainly because it matters:

- You're at 8 of 15 HP, prone, with no Rage and no Relentless Endurance left.
- You hold the prayer wheel in one hand. Your greataxe is strapped to your back, with two handaxes and three javelins at your belt.
- Two bandits and Harl have all acted this round, and it is now your turn.
- Being prone, you have disadvantage on your attack rolls. Melee attackers within 5 feet have advantage against you, and ranged attackers have disadvantage. Standing up costs half your movement.

The question of the key will have to wait. Harl's eyes are on the wheel in your hand, and he is shouting, "That's it! Take it from her!"

What does Grukka do?

entries.text:
A quick note from the DM: the tracker showed a leftover fight (Breach Bandits, Harl, you prone) that never happened in the story. You're in the barred, quiet nave, so I've cleared the stale fight and the prone condition.

The old priestess takes the prayer wheel from your hands as if it were a sleeping bird. In the lamplight she grips the brass cap, turns it a quarter against the way you've spun it your whole life, and pulls. The spindle slides out. Inside the hollow is a rolled strip of dark iron, no longer than a finger, notched like a tooth.

"Half a key," she says. "I have the other half, a ring under my shift. Together they open the door beneath the altar. One alone opens nothing, and that was the point. The founders split it so no single keeper could be forced, bribed or tricked into opening it."

She slides the spindle home and gives the wheel back. "As for what's below: they never said its name, only that it was a thing of the old wars that could not be killed, only bound. They didn't destroy it because they couldn't. Every blow they tried made it stronger. So they sealed it, and the temple was built on top so there would always be someone watching. The binding needs both halves of the key to open or to renew, and it weakens with each generation. I think Gaunt knows that. I think he wants it opened, not renewed."

She looks at you, and for the first time you see how old she is. "I took you in because you were left behind, Grukka, and I'd have done it anyway. But I gave you that wheel on the first night for a reason. You were the one thing in Thornwick no one would think to search."

You're at 8 of 15 HP, it's about 1 PM, and the baker's sons are on the river road for Merra. What does Grukka do?

Now the wheel. The priestess takes it from your scarred hands as if it were a sleeping bird, and her thumb finds a seam you have never noticed in a thousand spins. A half-turn against the prayer's direction, and the brass spindle slides free, a short rod of dark metal etched with fine teeth.

I gave it to you as a babe because no one would look for a key in a child's toy."

A quick note before the story continues: the tracker showed a fight in progress (some "Breach Bandits" and Harl, with you prone). Nothing like that happened at the table, so I've cleared it and kept the scene as it was. If you remember a rations or javelin count that differs from the sheet, tell me.

In the lamplit nave the old priestess closes your scarred fingers around the prayer wheel and turns it over so the base faces you. "Look at the foot. You've spun it a thousand times and never once looked."

You do. Beneath the worn brass cap, in the dull light, are grooves too regular to be wear: a ring of notches, like the teeth of a key.

"It was never a prayer wheel, child. It's the founders' half of the lock, made to look like a child's toy so no one would take it for what it was." She touches the carved altar-stone at the head of the nave. "My half is the seal-ring on this hand. The crypt door only answers when both are brought together, and by someone who can pray the old words over them. I have taught you most of those words without telling you why."

Then she tells you what lies below, and her voice drops. "The founders did not seal away a treasure. They sealed away a thing they could neither slay nor trust to rest: a warlord of the marches, bound alive in iron, who could not be killed because the border itself had made a pact with him. Destroying the chains would free him, so they left them, and set watchers over the door. Every priestess of this temple has been one of them." She looks at you. "Gaunt means to wake him. I don't know why, nor what he's promised. But a man who thanks a thug for bandaging you, and then waits patiently, is not a mere robber."
